sources.title: Jomon Prehistoric Sites in Northern Japan
sources.note: UNESCO synthesis of sedentary hunter-fisher-gatherer lifeways, varied environments, settlements and ritual places from about 13000 BCE to 400 BCE.

sources.title: What is Jomon Culture?
sources.note: Official heritage overview of the long chronology, six broad phases, pottery, villages, graves and regional variation.

sources.title: Jomon Prehistoric Sites in Northern Japan overview
sources.note: Official overview connecting sites, landforms, resources and changing lifeways across approximately 15000 to 2400 years ago.

sources.title: ICOMOS evaluation of Jomon Prehistoric Sites
sources.note: Expert evaluation of the seventeen-site series, sedentism, ritual practice, integrity and evidentiary limits.

sources.title: Research on the process of sedentarization in Jomon society
sources.note: National Museum of Japanese History research on chronology, settlement analysis and the difficulty of counting contemporaneous houses.

sources.title: When did the Jomon period begin?
sources.note: National Museum exhibition on early pottery dating, paste, food residues, regional traditions and scientific methods.

sources.title: The World of Jomon Wetlands
sources.note: National Museum exhibition on exceptional preservation of textiles, baskets, wooden objects, bows, canoes, bark and lacquer.

sources.title: Opening Doors to the Jomon Period
sources.note: National Museum exhibition evidence for bone tools, salt making, jade, lacquer and ornament production.

sources.title: Sannai-Maruyama Site archaeological guide
sources.note: Official site dossier for 3900 to 2200 BCE houses, graves, storage, craft production and long-distance materials.

sources.title: Sannai-Maruyama remains and dwellings
sources.note: Aomori site authority description of ordinary and large pit dwellings and reconstructed building evidence.

sources.title: Summary of each Jomon archaeological site
sources.note: Official comparative catalogue of settlement layouts, burials, food remains, tools, ritual structures and site-specific dates.

sources.title: Kitakogane Site
sources.note: Official site account of a coastal settlement, shell midden, food remains, burials, spring and deposited grinding stones.

sources.title: Oyu Stone Circles
sources.note: Official site account of two large stone circles, graves, buildings, storage and solstitial alignment around 2000 to 1500 BCE.

sources.title: Korekawa Site
sources.note: Official site evidence for later lacquered wood, food remains and water-soaking treatment of horse chestnuts.

sources.title: The Prayers and Hearts of the Jomon People
sources.note: Hokkaido Digital Museum discussion of clay tablets bearing children’s footprints and cautious ritual interpretation.

sources.title: Earliest evidence for the use of pottery
sources.note: Peer-reviewed residue study detecting aquatic processing in very early Japanese pottery and explaining chemical evidence.

sources.title: Long-term use of pottery among hunter-gatherers
sources.note: Peer-reviewed lipid analysis of Torihama pottery alongside plant, animal and tool evidence, with clear residue limitations.

sources.title: Organic residue analysis and environmental change in Jomon pottery
sources.note: Peer-reviewed biomarker study showing how vessel residues track foods while leaving many plant uses archaeologically quiet.

sources.title: Plant management and environmental interaction in Jomon Japan
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archaeological synthesis of chestnut and lacquer tree management without equating it with rice-field farming.

sources.title: Jomon plant domestication and cultivation
sources.note: Peer-reviewed review of changing seed size in soybean, adzuki bean and barnyard grass and the cultivation debate.

sources.title: Agriculture and plant use in Jomon Japan
sources.note: Peer-reviewed warning that agricultural claims require direct plant evidence rather than attractive but unsupported stories.

sources.title: Early Jomon lacquer technology
sources.note: Academic analysis of layered lacquer, pigments, additives and skilled production in Early Jomon contexts.

sources.title: The Beauty of Japanese Lacquerware
sources.note: Japanese government cultural overview of prehistoric lacquer coating, adhesion, durability, water resistance and handling risks.

sources.title: Middle Jomon obsidian exchange networks in Kanto
sources.note: Peer-reviewed geochemical sourcing of Kozushima obsidian and changing network connectivity through Middle and Late Jomon.

sources.title: Origin of Jomon jade artifacts
sources.note: Mineralogical study linking jade ornaments and tools to the Itoigawa source region in central Honshu.

sources.title: Jomon bone fishhook
sources.note: Museum object record contextualizing bone fishhooks, needles, harpoons and fishing within shell-midden lifeways.

sources.title: Tools for hunting, fishing, and gathering
sources.note: Tokyo National Museum records for bows, arrows, hooks, harpoons and grinding tools used in varied subsistence work.

sources.title: Dental caries in Jomon people
sources.note: Peer-reviewed multi-site study of cavities and major regional and chronological differences in diet-related dental disease.

sources.title: Periodontal disease in Jomon skeletal remains
sources.note: Peer-reviewed skeletal study of periodontal disease, age patterns and regional limits in the available sample.

sources.title: Ancient DNA analysis of a Jomon double burial
sources.note: Peer-reviewed finding that one closely placed adult and child were not a mother-child pair, cautioning against visual kinship assumptions.

sources.title: Unearthing Fluctuating Wealth Inequality
sources.note: Cambridge archaeological study of 1150 dwellings finding low measured Late Jomon floor-area inequality while stressing proxy limits.

sources.title: Ancient Jomon of Japan, chapter one
sources.note: Academic synthesis of subsistence-settlement systems, social organization, terminology and changing archaeological interpretations.

sources.title: DNA Tells the Story of the Jomon People
sources.note: University of Tokyo museum explanation that no written Jomon records survive and that bones and DNA answer different questions.

sources.title: The origin of Jomon pottery as an archaeological name
sources.note: University museum history of Morse, cord-marked pottery and the modern scholarly label rather than an ancient self-name.

sources.title: Paleoparasitology of historical toilets and mummies in South Korea
sources.note: Peer-reviewed 2026 comparison noting uncertain Jomon toilet form, coprolites in shell middens and current parasite evidence.

sources.title: Human Life and Death as Told by Ancient Bones
sources.note: University of Tokyo museum exhibition on Jomon activity, injuries, teeth, burial and limits of skeletal interpretation.

sources.title: Violence in the prehistoric period of Japan
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archipelago-wide skeletal study finding low and spatially restricted violent mortality while avoiding a claim of zero conflict.

sources.title: Japan’s oldest Jomon dog burials
sources.note: Keio University project documenting radiocarbon dating, recovery and analysis of deliberately buried Jomon dogs.

sources.title: Hunting dogs as environmental adaptations in Jomon Japan
sources.note: Peer-reviewed interpretation of later dog burials and canine help tracking wounded game in forest environments.

sources.title: Regional divergences in Jomon population dynamics
sources.note: Peer-reviewed radiocarbon study showing eastern regional booms and declines rather than one archipelago-wide demographic curve.

sources.title: Ancient genomics and the Jomon-Yayoi transition
sources.note: Peer-reviewed genomic and chronological review of migration, mixture, rice agriculture and disputed transition dates.

sources.title: The transition from Jomon to Yayoi as a regional process
sources.note: Peer-reviewed account of a time-transgressive transition involving farmers and hunter-gatherers rather than a single replacement event.

sources.title: The spatiotemporal spread of rice farming in prehistoric Japan
sources.note: Peer-reviewed chronology placing early wet rice in northern Kyushu and tracing a discontinuous spread eastward.

sources.title: Culinary continuity across the Jomon-Yayoi transition
sources.note: Peer-reviewed pottery-residue evidence for regional persistence and change in cooking as crops and farming spread.

sources.title: Human paleodemography and paleoecology of the North Pacific Rim
sources.note: Peer-reviewed sequence from Jomon through Epi-Jomon, Satsumon and Okhotsk traditions toward historically recognizable Ainu communities.

sources.title: Genomic insights into ancestry in the Southern Ryukyu Islands
sources.note: Peer-reviewed evidence for Jomon-related ancestry alongside distinct northern and southern Ryukyuan cultural trajectories and later mixture.

sources.title: Reconstructing the Human Population History of East Asia
sources.note: Cambridge synthesis of ancient genomic links and later admixture among archipelago populations, Ainu and Ryukyuans.

proposedOverrides.summary: A regionally varied archaeological culture of settlement, pottery, fishing, hunting, plant management, craft and exchange. The 1500 BCE atlas endpoint is a relabeled seam, not Jōmon extinction.
